A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MotionPrompt and contain complete main texts and supplementary material. Text, equations, tables and figures can be matched across revisions and relocations. The embedded animation frames also match.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation benchmarks, a 20-participant user study, ablations, discriminator-transfer experiments and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and reports a replacement 100-participant user study, quantitative loss ablations and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: MotionPrompt retains the same token-optimization procedure, optical-flow discriminator, TV loss and embedding-distance penalty. Algorithms 1–2 and default hyperparameters are unchanged. The embedding penalty discussed more extensively in v2 was already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use DAVIS and WebVid for discriminator training, VBench prompts for text-to-video evaluation, and DynamiCrafter for image-to-video examples. The enlarged user study changes sampling and assessment procedures without establishing a new task, domain or participant population.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Lavie, AnimateDiff, VideoCrafter2, DynamiCrafter and the retained FreeInit configurations. Newly cited video-generation methods are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The user study changes from 20 participants rating nine videos on three 1–5 scales to 100 participants comparing 90 video pairs for natural, smooth motion, with A/B/Both responses (Section 4.2; Appendix A.3). v2 also adds loss-weight controls and computational-cost evaluation. The main 800-prompt, 50-step benchmark protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's qualitative loss-component examples in Figure 5 are replaced by quantitative tests of discriminator-loss removal, TV weighting and embedding-penalty removal in v2 Table 3. Appendix B.3 adds computational-overhead analysis. Existing token, iteration, optimization-range, discriminator-transfer and FreeInit analyses remain; moving discriminator transfer into Section 5.2 is not a new experiment.

E5.justification: New Appendix B.3 explicitly reports averaging computational measurements over 100 generations. This adds a measurement-aggregation count, without establishing additional training runs. No new confidence intervals, significance tests or multiseed benchmark estimates are supplied.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces three mean-rating comparisons with MotionPrompt win/tie/loss results, including win rates of 66.5%, 55.1% and 53.0% against AnimateDiff, Lavie and VideoCrafter2. These are different assessments, not comparable performance gains. v2 adds loss-ablation scores and baseline/MotionPrompt costs of 18.94/50.94 seconds and 11.38/35.60 GiB. Main Table 1 and retained appendix benchmark values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, objectives and underlying reasoning remain unchanged. Edits to alpha bars and a missing denoised-estimate hat repair notation in existing equations; no substantive derivation, assumption, theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: inference-time prompt optimization guided by an optical-flow discriminator improves temporal coherence without retraining the diffusion model, while preserving prompt semantics.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation linking embedding regularization to avoiding departure from the model's trained text space, interprets loss-weight tradeoffs and asserts hyperparameter robustness. Section 4.1 also argues that clean training videos and denoised inference estimates provide distinct discriminator inputs. The existing physical-plausibility and generation-time limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents Prolific recruitment, the revised study question and response options, clarifies clean-video training versus denoised-estimate inference, and supplies measured memory and generation-time costs. Discriminator architecture, optimizer settings, evaluation hyperparameters, hardware and project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds citations to Align Your Latents, CogVideo and CogVideoX. These modestly broaden background coverage without changing the paper's novelty claim or its positioning relative to prompt optimization and optical-flow guidance.

P1.justification: Section 5 is reorganized, discriminator generalization moves from Appendix B into the main text, and the study and loss-analysis passages are rewritten. Author affiliations/contact information and acknowledgements are updated. Most introductory, methodological and concluding prose remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains a notation legend and revised rendering. Table 2 is redesigned, Table 3 gains a loss-weight block, and the discriminator-transfer table moves into the main text. The qualitative loss figure is removed and a computational-cost display is added; most qualitative figures are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: The broader paired motion study, quantitative loss controls and explicit resource costs make the evidence and practical tradeoffs easier to assess. Benefits are limited by removing human ratings of overall quality and text alignment. Also, Table 3 does not support the stated monotonic TV-weight trend, and the unchanged description of generation time as only slightly higher understates the reported 2.7-fold cost. Overall, the added evidence and transparency provide a modest net improvement.
